A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ACT research paper, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. The complete material supports direct comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation, criticism, and downstream-training experiments in Sections 4–5, with robustness tests and additional comparisons in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 3, the stability analyses, and the supplementary experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The annotation–criticism–human-correction pipeline, prompt strategies, sampling rules, and ACT loss remain unchanged, including the implementation formulations in Appendices C and E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six main datasets and the same AlleNoise and CIFAR10-LT scenarios in Appendix G.3.3. Correcting the irony description and AlleNoise capitalization does not change coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated model families and comparator sets are unchanged. Tables 6–7 retain CDI, pseudo labeling, and active pseudo labeling; Tables 10–11 retain the same random-sampling and criticizer comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, metrics, model configurations, human budgets, training procedures, and supplementary experimental settings are unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–G.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same stability and sampling analyses, human-budget sensitivity tests, biased and long-tail evaluations, critic error analyses, annotator–criticizer ablation, and cost analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain single-run reporting for the main annotation explorations, five-repeat stability tests in Appendix B, mean±standard-deviation reporting over five downstream runs, and the seed-42 disclosure in Appendix A.2.

E6.justification: Numerical results and reported findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, ACT thresholding achieves 87.95±0.35% on CIFAR10 in Table 3 and 90.14±1.79% on AlleNoise in Table 8 in both versions.

T1.justification: The AQG and ABS definitions, Proposition 5.1, Theorem 5.2, their assumptions and Appendix D proofs, and the Appendix E loss derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope, including seven empirical insights and the claim of a downstream performance gap below 2% on most benchmarks while saving up to 90% of human costs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of criticism, sampling, and downstream performance are unchanged. The classification-task limitation, proposed extensions to complex tasks, and ethical discussion are also retained.

D1.justification: References [34–35] replace direct Qwen-VL model and InternVL repository links with report citations, changing the supplied resource pointers. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, dataset-access information, and training instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A limited set of cited sources changes: reference [34] switches from Qwen-VL to the Qwen2.5-VL technical report, and [30] now identifies the GPT-4o system card. Research positioning remains unchanged. Most other edits update bibliographic metadata; removing the duplicate MILO entry does not remove that work, which remains reference [19].

P1.justification: v2 revises bibliography wording and publication details, fixes 'rony' to 'irony' in Table 4, and standardizes AlleNoise capitalization. Section structure and scientific prose remain unchanged. Appendix G.1 introduces an unresolved '[?]' citation where v1 had [63].

P2.justification: Expanded reference entries change line wrapping and page breaks within bibliography pages 11–15. Figures 1–13, table structures, captions, and scientific-content placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves source documentation: references [33–34] explicitly identify LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2.5-VL, matching the models already specified in Section 3, and many entries provide fuller publication details. The benefit is limited by the new unresolved citation in Appendix G.1 and removal of some direct resource links. Scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged.
